Last week, Apple disclosed that its iPad revenue in the June quarter declined 5% year over year. A new report now places this decline within the broader context of the tablet market in Q2 2026. Details below.

Global Tablet Shipments Fall

According to a new report from research firm Omdia (cited by MacMagazine), global tablet shipments in Q2 2026 fell to 35.5 million units, down 9.9% from the same period last year.

The report noted that despite a 7.5% drop in shipments, Apple remained the market leader with 13.5 million iPads shipped and a 37.8% market share. Samsung came second with 5.8 million units shipped and a 16.3% share; Lenovo ranked third with 11.1%, Xiaomi fourth with 8%, and Huawei fifth with 7.7%.

Among the top five vendors, Lenovo was the only brand to record growth, with shipments rising 27.1% compared to Q2 2025.

Omdia pointed out that vendors outside the top five collectively accounted for 19.1% of total shipments, with their combined shipments falling 23.5% year over year.

Below is Omdia Research Manager Himani Mukka's response to the report:

Mukka added that, amid ongoing component supply tightness, "it is difficult for vendors to fully prioritise tablets." Instead, they expect to "concentrate limited resources on flagship and high-end models, further skewing the product mix toward premium devices."
